analyst_view.overall: Early view: a matchday-23 game brought forward because both clubs play February's Supercopa, and it lands at the end of a brutal week for Real Sociedad (Crystal Palace on 26 November, Sevilla on the 29th). Mourinho's Madrid have won eight in a row, Mbappé has scored in seven straight games and they have conceded 10 in 12; they then go to Athletic and Arsenal within a week, and Mourinho is already complaining about the schedule.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals, with Madrid expected to score twice. That fits: Madrid scored three at both Racing and Valencia and Real Sociedad have conceded 20 in 12, but a tired home side without Barrenetxea may not add much at the other end. I stay around 3, most of it from Madrid.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners. Real Sociedad's last two games had 13 corners each, but Madrid's away wins at Racing and Valencia produced only 8 and 7 as they controlled play through the middle. Those pull in opposite directions, so I stay around 10.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.6 cards. Madrid took three yellows in each of their last two big away games, and Real Sociedad's Aramburu and Yangel Herrera are one booking from bans; a tired home side chasing Madrid's counters could foul late on. I stay around 4-5.

shots.text: The numbers say 27 shots, 15 of them Madrid's. Madrid took 22 at Racing and 19 at Valencia while allowing 10 and 4, and Real Sociedad's own games have high volume (28 against Rayo). I lean a little higher, around 28-29.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.7 on target. Madrid put 11 of 19 on target at Valencia with Valverde, Güler and Mbappé all scoring, but Real Sociedad managed 3 from 17 against Rayo and will be tired. I stay close to the number, with Madrid providing most of it.
